assign.outcome:
**Docs tier audited at 5 widths (400–3440), before round.** 13 pages: `/framework/`, its six sections' landing pages (`core`, `ext`, `styles`, `ui`, `ux`, `web`—substituted `/web/` since `/framework/web/` from the shared brief does not exist), and one `doc/` page per section. 3520 findings (`strip` 534, `touching` 1493, `padding-fat` 564, `padding-thin` 823, `ratio` 94, `no-growth` 12) in [`findings.json`](/framework/ai/2026-09-05/spacing-audit-c/findings.json). Ten crops of the worst, `shots/before/crop-C-*.jpg`.

**Headline: the `<details>`/`<summary>` ‘Readme’ toggle repeats the owner's exact complaint** — 601.6px wide, 57.8px of content, a 10.4x empty strip, identical on `/framework/`, `core/`, `ext/`, `styles/`, `ui/`, `ux/` at 1280px (![](shots/before/crop-C-206.jpg)). And **12 of 13 pages barely grow with the viewport** (median sibling gap 3440÷1280 ≈ 1.2x, against a 2.69x viewport growth) — the docs tier's prose spacing is effectively fixed regardless of screen width.

Reusable script: `C:/Users/mike/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/c--Code-lew42-monorepo/e938046a-4711-446c-9b36-6713cd4e869f/scratchpad/spacing-audit-c.mjs` (takes the round as its one argument, unchanged for the after run).

**Left open:** which `doc/` page ‘counts’ as each section's first for `core`/`ext`/`styles` is a judgment call — those three sections aren't `Doc`-type pages themselves (no Docs tab of their own), so I picked the first `Doc`-type descendant on each section's own recommended reading path. Fixing nothing — evidence only, per brief.

assign.now: round 2: ran script with after, wrote findings-after.json + shots/after; verdicted the 10 before-crops

log.msg: C-206/C-871/C-1151/C-1492/C-1947/C-2542 FIXED: the Readme <summary> toggle now hugs its content on all six pages -- 601.6/57.8 (10.4x) at 1280 is now 72.2-99.2/57.8 (about 1.25x). Verified the judges own 3440 example directly: /framework/ summary went 720/69.2 -> 86.4/69.2, exact match.
C-13 FIXED: page-preview-link on /framework/ at 400px went 324/53.8 (6.02x) -> 60.2/53.8 (1.0x), a clean hug.

C-1795 and C-2247 UNCHANGED: the ui-tree-row control strip on /framework/ui/ was not touched by this fix -- still 244/17.6 (13.84x) at 400px and 371/36.8 (9.75x, was 10.08x) at 3440px. A different pattern from the <summary> one; the owners complaint still applies here.
C-96 UNCHANGED: the mobile sidebar/page-content touching (0px gap at 400px on /framework/) is exactly the same after -- not addressed by this rounds CSS change.

Findings by kind before->after: strip 534->260, ratio 94->44, no-growth 12->5, padding-thin 823->74 (all improved). touching 1493->1498 and padding-fat 564->569 look worse by raw count but the UNIQUE (kind,url,selector) sets are identical for touching (844 before, 844 after, 0 new/0 gone) -- pure width-threshold noise, not a real regression.

padding-fat genuinely gained 5 new instances, but all 5 are the SAME element: the newly-hugged Readme <summary> on /framework/ui/ at all five widths (padding now 16.8-21.6px against its own shrunk 66-85px width = 25.3%, just over the 20% threshold). A side effect of hugging tightly, not a fresh visual problem -- flagging for the judge to see, not calling it a regression.
median growth (1280->3440) across my 13 pages: 1.2x before -> 1.75x after, a real improvement though still short of the 2.69x viewport growth.

p75/p90 check on /framework/ at 3440 (after): p75=10.8 (was 12.03 at 1280, essentially flat), p90=54 (was 30.08 at 1280, a genuine 1.8x growth well above the median 1.2x). This CONFIRMS the direction of the judges claim (gains concentrate at the top of the distribution, not the median) but does NOT match their specific cited numbers (24.4 -> 46.2) -- my p75 does not show that growth, only p90 shows a comparably large jump. Before-round p75/p90 was not computed (out of scope for that run), so I cannot directly verify their before number either.

assign.outcome: **Round 2 (after) verified the fix.** findings-after.json: 2450 findings (down from 3520). The headline strip finding is FIXED sitewide: the Readme <summary> toggle hugs its content on all six /framework/ landing pages (601.6/57.8, 10.4x, at 1280 -> ~72-99/57.8, ~1.25x); independently confirmed the judges own 3440 example (720/69.2 -> 86.4/69.2, exact match). Of my ten before-crops: 7 fixed, 3 unchanged (two ui-tree-row control strips the fix did not touch, and the mobile sidebar/page-content 0px touching). Median growth 1280->3440 improved 1.2x -> 1.75x. What did NOT improve: touching (1493->1498) and padding-fat (564->569) look worse by raw count, but touchings unique pairs are identical (844/844, 0 new) -- noise, not a regression; padding-fats 5 new instances are all the SAME already-fixed Readme toggle at 5 widths (its own padding is now ~25% of its newly-shrunk width, just over the 20% rule) -- a side effect of hugging tightly, not a fresh problem. My own p75/p90 check does not corroborate the judges specific claimed number (24.4->46.2 at p75) -- I measure p75 essentially flat (12.03->10.8) with the real growth at p90 (30.08->54, 1.8x) instead, confirming the DIRECTION of their claim but not the exact figures.
